Apply the **Unit Digit Method** to identify the result quickly.

Sum of unit digits: 3 + 2 − 1 + (1 + 1) − 8 + 3

⇒ (3 + 2 + 2 + 3) − (1 + 8) = 10 − 9 = 1

Since the unit digit of the final value is **1**, the answer is 121.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 73 + 92 − 61 + (41 + 21) − 78 + 33

Follow the **BODMAS** rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction) to simplify the expression:

⇒ 73 + 92 − 61 + 62 − 78 + 33

⇒ (73 + 92 + 62 + 33) − (61 + 78)

⇒ 260 − 139

⇒ 121

**∴ The correct answer is 121.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The rule defines the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**. Always solve terms inside brackets first.

Grouping Method

For faster calculation, group all **positive terms** together and all **negative terms** together before performing the final subtraction.

Unit Digit Technique

This shortcut helps eliminate incorrect options by focusing only on the last digit of each number in the arithmetic operation.

questions.question: 79 + 29 - (36 ÷ 6) + 42 of 1 + 13 - 24 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **VBODMAS**: solve brackets and **'of'** operations first.

Calculate **(36 ÷ 6) = 6** and **42 of 1 = 42**.

Group positive and negative terms: **(79 + 29 + 42 + 13) − (6 + 24)**.

Final sum: **163 − 30 = 133**.

**∴ The correct answer is 133.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 79 + 29 − (36 ÷ 6) + 42 of 1 + 13 − 24

**Formula Used:** Simplify the expression using the **BODMAS** rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 79 + 29 − 6 + 42 of 1 + 13 − 24 (Solving Bracket first)

⇒ 79 + 29 − 6 + 42 + 13 − 24 (Solving **'of'**: 42 × 1)

⇒ 108 − 6 + 42 + 13 − 24 (Addition from left to right)

⇒ 102 + 42 + 13 − 24

⇒ 144 + 13 − 24

⇒ 157 − 24

⇒ 133

**∴ The correct answer is 133.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

This acronym defines the priority of operations: **Bracket** (), **Of** (order/powers), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Priority of Of Operator

In mathematical expressions, **'of'** is a multiplication operation that must be completed **before** any division or standard multiplication.

Negative Number Rule

When multiple subtractions are present, they can be combined as: **−a − b = −(a + b)**.

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 168, and their HCF is 14. If one of the numbers is 42, find the other number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of two numbers = **LCM × HCF**

42 × Second Number = 168 × 14

Second Number = (168 × 14) ÷ 42

Second Number = 168 ÷ 3 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** = 168

⇒ **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** = 14

⇒ **First Number** (n₁) = 42

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = **LCM** × **HCF**

n₁ × n₂ = LCM(n₁, n₂) × HCF(n₁, n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f15ee4db0c87022fdaab9074df49ba097096ea2558d38d176b0d2214c5cd20c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the other number be **x**.

⇒ 42 × x = 168 × 14

⇒ x = (168 × 14) ÷ 42

⇒ x = 2352 ÷ 42

⇒ x = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF Property

The **Highest Common Factor** of two numbers always divides their **LCM** exactly.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are **co-prime**, their **HCF is 1** and their **LCM** is equal to the product of the two numbers.

Product Rule Constraint

The formula **Product of Numbers = LCM × HCF** is strictly valid only for **two numbers** and does not apply directly to three or more numbers.

questions.question: (4.2)² × 4.2 - 3 × 0.2 × (4.2)² + 3 × 4.2 × (0.2)² - (0.2)³ = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the expression as the **algebraic identity**: a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³ = (a − b)³.

Here, a = 4.2 and b = 0.2.

The expression simplifies to (4.2 − 0.2)³.

⇒ 4³ = 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** (4.2)² × 4.2 − 3 × 0.2 × (4.2)² + 3 × 4.2 × (0.2)² − (0.2)³

**Formula Used:** (a − b)³ = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³

⇒ Rewrite the terms to match the identity: (4.2)³ − 3(4.2)²(0.2) + 3(4.2)(0.2)² − (0.2)³

⇒ Let **a = 4.2** and **b = 0.2**.

⇒ Expression = (4.2 − 0.2)³

⇒ Expression = (4.0)³

⇒ 4 × 4 × 4 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube of Sum Identity

(a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b).

Difference of Two Cubes

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Sum of Two Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).

questions.question: If x=sqrt{484}div sqrt{121}+sqrt{64}, then what is the value of x²?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify **perfect square roots**: √484 = 22, √121 = 11, and √64 = 8.

Substitute in equation: x = (22 ÷ 11) + 8

Solve for x: x = 2 + 8 = 10

Calculate **x²**: 10 × 10 = 100

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x = √484 ÷ √121 + √64

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** (Division before Addition) and Square root values.

⇒ √484 = 22

⇒ √121 = 11

⇒ √64 = 8

⇒ x = 22 ÷ 11 + 8

⇒ x = 2 + 8

⇒ x = 10

⇒ x² = 10²

⇒ x² = 100

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares and Roots

Memorizing **squares** up to 30 helps in fast calculation (e.g., 20² = 400, 22² = 484, 25² = 625).

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the sequence: Brackets, Orders (Powers/Roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Square Root Estimation

For √484, since the last digit is 4, the root ends in 2 or 8. Since 20² = 400 and 30² = 900, the root is 22.

questions.question: (5+sqrt{3})²+(5-sqrt{3})²-40=?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the algebraic identity: **(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)**.

Here, **a = 5** and **b = √3**.

Sum of squares = 2 × (5² + (√3)²) = 2 × (25 + 3) = 56.

Required value = 56 − 40 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** (5 + √3)² + (5 − √3)² − 40

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

⇒ Expansion of (5 + √3)² = 5² + (√3)² + 2 × 5 × √3 = 25 + 3 + 10√3 = **28 + 10√3**

⇒ Expansion of (5 − √3)² = 5² + (√3)² − 2 × 5 × √3 = 25 + 3 − 10√3 = **28 − 10√3**

⇒ Total = (28 + 10√3) + (28 − 10√3) − 40

⇒ Total = 28 + 28 + 10√3 − 10√3 − 40

⇒ Total = 56 − 40

⇒ 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Algebraic Identities

The identity **(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)** is a quick way to sum the squares of binomials with identical terms.

Subtraction of Binomial Squares

Similarly, **(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab** is used when the terms are being subtracted instead of added.

Difference of Two Squares

The product of **(a + b)** and **(a − b)** always results in **a² − b²**, which is useful for rationalizing denominators.

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 3 and 8?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check **Divisibility by 8** first (last three digits) then **Divisibility by 3** (sum of digits).

For **5448**: Last three digits **448** are divisible by **8** (448 ÷ 8 = 56).

Sum of digits **5+4+4+8 = 21**, which is divisible by **3** (21 ÷ 3 = 7).

Both conditions are satisfied for the number **5448**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5448.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (1) 5448, (2) 5240, (3) 5560, (4) 6170.

**Rules:** A number is divisible by **3** if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3. A number is divisible by **8** if the **last three digits** are divisible by 8.

⇒ **Option 1: 5448**

⇒ Sum = 5 + 4 + 4 + 8 = 21 (Divisible by 3 because 21 ÷ 3 = 7)

⇒ Last 3 digits = 448 (Divisible by 8 because 448 ÷ 8 = 56)

⇒ **Option 2: 5240**

⇒ Sum = 5 + 2 + 4 + 0 = 11 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ **Option 3: 5560**

⇒ Sum = 5 + 5 + 6 + 0 = 16 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ **Option 4: 6170**

⇒ Sum = 6 + 1 + 7 + 0 = 14 (Not divisible by 3)

**∴ The correct answer is 5448.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its **last two digits** is divisible by 4 or ends in 00.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of all its digits** is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 11

The difference between the **sum of digits at odd places** and **even places** must be either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: There is a rectangular garden of 180 metres × 70 metres. A path of width 4 metres is build outside the garden. What is the area (in square metre) of the path?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **path** built **outside** a **rectangular garden**:

Area of path = 2w × (L + B + 2w)

Where L = 180 m, B = 70 m, and w = 4 m.

Area = 2 × 4 × (180 + 70 + 2 × 4) = 8 × (250 + 8)

Area = 8 × 258 = 2064 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 2064 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length (L) of the **rectangular garden** = 180 m

Breadth (B) of the garden = 70 m

Width of the **path** = 4 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25c607c04cd65aa1116f2f5b9addf66f04131badfcea1c976116fb87180436a7.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of path = (Area including path) − (Area of garden)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Outer Length = 180 + 4 + 4 = 188 m

⇒ Outer Breadth = 70 + 4 + 4 = 78 m

⇒ Inner Area (Garden) = 180 × 70 = 12600 m²

⇒ Outer Area (Total) = 188 × 78 = 14664 m²

⇒ Area of **path** = 14664 − 12600

⇒ Area of **path** = 2064 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 2064 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Path Inside a Rectangle

If the path is built inside the rectangular field, the area is calculated as Area = 2w × (L + B − 2w).

Cross-roads Area

Area of two paths of width 'w' crossing each other at right angles in the middle of a field = w × (L + B − w).

Perimeter including Path

The perimeter of the outer boundary after adding a path of width 'w' is 2 × (L + B + 4w).

questions.question: There are two numbers such that the first number is half of the second number. If their average is 66, then what is the first number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **1st number** to **2ⁿd number** = 1 : 2

**Sum** of two numbers = Average × 2 = 66 × 2 = 132

Total ratio parts = 1 + 2 = 3 parts

3 parts = 132 ⇒ 1 part = 132 ÷ 3 = 44

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average** of two numbers = 66

**First number** = 1/2 × **Second number**

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of observations) ÷ (Number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5fe07282a74ce49887043240d7cc7fea286d2e408b67bd9cc3afc650ff647514.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **second number** be 2x.

⇒ **First number** = (1/2) × 2x = x

⇒ Average = (x + 2x) ÷ 2 = 66

⇒ 3x ÷ 2 = 66

⇒ 3x = 66 × 2

⇒ 3x = 132

⇒ x = 132 ÷ 3

⇒ x = 44

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of n Numbers

The average is the central value of a set of data, calculated as Sum of all values ÷ Total count of values.

Sum and Average Relation

Total Sum = Average × Number of observations. This is used to find individual values when ratios are given.

Ratio to Value Conversion

If a total **S** is divided in ratio a:b, then the first part is [a ÷ (a+b)] × **S**.

questions.question: Average of 14 numbers is 'm'. Average of 5 numbers among them is 23. Average of the remaining numbers is 37. What is the value of 'm'?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Assume **base average** is 23 for all 14 numbers. The remaining 9 numbers are 37 − 23 = 14 higher than the base. Total **surplus** = 9 × 14 = 126. Distribute this surplus over all 14 numbers: 126 ÷ 14 = 9. Value of **m** = Base + Increase = 23 + 9 = 32. **∴ The correct answer is 32.**

questions.question: There is a rectangular floor of size 525 cm × 700 cm. The floor is to tiled with largest square tiles. How many such tiles will be required?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The side of the **largest square tile** is the **HCF** of the floor dimensions. Side = HCF(525, 700) = 175 cm. Number of tiles along length = 700 ÷ 175 = 4. Number of tiles along breadth = 525 ÷ 175 = 3. Total tiles required = 4 × 3 = 12. **∴ The correct answer is 12.**

questions.question: If 2/5 of 60 percent of a number is 420, then what is the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **60%** to a fraction: 60/100 = 3/5.

Total fraction of the number = 2/5 × 3/5 = 6/25.

Given: 6 units = 420.

1 unit = 420 ÷ 6 = 70.

The total number (25 units) = 25 × 70 = 1750.

**∴ The correct answer is 1750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fraction part = 2/5

Percentage part = 60%

Value of the result = 420

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13044ee30284f8b064416439fbf9cd83c80ce26815aa86b1384468e59dcfbbdf.png] 

**Calculation:**

Let the **number** be x.

⇒ (2/5) × 60% × x = 420

⇒ (2/5) × (60/100) × x = 420

⇒ (2/5) × (3/5) × x = 420

⇒ (6/25) × x = 420

⇒ x = (420 × 25) ÷ 6

⇒ x = 70 × 25

⇒ x = 1750

**∴ The correct answer is 1750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage to a fraction, divide by 100. Example: 20% = 20/100 = 1/5; 40% = 2/5; 60% = 3/5; 80% = 4/5.

Concept of "Of" in Mathematics

The word **"of"** represents the multiplication operation (×) in BODMAS/VBODMAS rules for simplification.

Successive Fractions

When taking a fraction of another fraction, the net multiplier is the product of the individual fractions: (a/b) of (c/d) = (a×c)/(b×d).

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price of an article is Rs. 720. Loss percentage is 30 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Loss Percentage** = 30% = 3/10 (where 3 units is **Loss** and 10 units is **Cost Price**).

The difference between **CP** and **SP** when there is a loss is the **Loss** itself.

Given: 3 units = ₹720 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹240.

**Selling Price (SP)** = CP − Loss = 10 units − 3 units = 7 units.

SP = 7 × 240 = ₹1680.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Difference (**CP** − **SP**) = ₹720

**Loss Percentage** = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = **Cost Price (CP)** − **Selling Price (SP)**

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4ccbfbd0e0fa66201e7abb64b72305683406d850e5df59e64d07802460ca28a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Loss** = ₹720

⇒ 30 = (720 ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ CP = (720 × 100) ÷ 30

⇒ CP = 24 × 100 = ₹2400

⇒ SP = CP − Loss

⇒ SP = 2400 − 720

⇒ SP = ₹1680

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Relation

When **Selling Price (SP)** is greater than **Cost Price (CP)**, there is a profit: Profit = SP − CP. When CP > SP, there is a loss: Loss = CP − SP.

Percentage Calculation Base

Profit % and Loss % are always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless specifically mentioned otherwise in the question.

Direct SP Formula

SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100 for loss cases, and SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 for profit cases.

questions.question: An article is sold for a profit of 50 percent. What is the ratio of the selling price of the article to the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit percentage** of 50% can be written as the fraction 1/2.

In this fraction, the denominator represents the **Cost Price (CP)** and the numerator represents the **Profit**.

Let **CP** = 2 units and **Profit** = 1 unit.

**Selling Price (SP)** = **CP** + **Profit** = 2 + 1 = 3 units.

The required **Ratio** of **SP** to **CP** is 3 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Profit percentage** = 50%

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** × (100 + **Profit%**) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5c1394a0f039a23a8672a11bd1bd3af649b9f4ae14bbe5ed824ec40486d30b1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be 100 units.

⇒ **Profit** = 50% of 100 = 50 units.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = **CP** + **Profit**

⇒ **SP** = 100 + 50 = 150 units.

⇒ Required **Ratio** = **SP** : **CP**

⇒ **Ratio** = 150 : 100

⇒ Dividing both sides by 50, we get 3 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Formulas

Profit = **Selling Price** − **Cost Price**. Loss = **Cost Price** − **Selling Price**. Both are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price and Selling Price

**Selling Price** = **Marked Price** − **Discount**. Discount % = (**Discount** ÷ **Marked Price**) × 100.

Successive Discount

Two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are equivalent to a single discount of (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 35/20 of the first number. The second number is what percent of the first number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of (**Sum** : **First number**) = 35 : 20.

**Second number** = **Sum** − **First number** = 35 − 20 = 15 units.

Required **Percentage** = (15 ÷ 20) × 100 = 75%.

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Sum of two numbers** = (35 ÷ 20) × **First number**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43e54e54531ea54e14fcae6a9b508b235cb2c6584027b7ed25fdb969c84f5ae2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **First number** be 20x.

⇒ **Sum** = (35 ÷ 20) × 20x = 35x.

⇒ Let the **Second number** be y.

⇒ 20x + y = 35x

⇒ y = 35x − 20x = 15x

⇒ Required **Percentage** = (**Second number** ÷ **First number**) × 100

⇒ **Percentage** = (15x ÷ 20x) × 100

⇒ **Percentage** = (3 ÷ 4) × 100 = 75%

**∴ The correct answer is 75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base Value Identification

In percentage questions, the word 'of' or 'than' identifies the base value (denominator). Here, it is the **First number**.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Common fractions: 1/4 = 25%, 1/2 = 50%, 3/4 = 75%, and 1/5 = 20%.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage = (Part ÷ Whole) × 100. If the Part is the difference, it represents the percentage increase/decrease.

questions.question: A pipe can empty a tank in 20 hours. What part of this tank will it empty in 5 hours?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time to **empty** the **tank** = 20 hr.

Work done in **1 hour** = 1/20 of the **tank**.

Work done in **5 hours** = 5 × (1/20) = 1/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time taken by **pipe** to empty the **tank** = 20 hr.

Formula: **Part of tank emptied** = (Time given) ÷ (Total time to empty)

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Emptying Pipe
 20 hr
 20 units
 20 ÷ 20 = 1 unit/hr
 
 

⇒ **Total Capacity** of the tank = 20 units (LCM of 20).

⇒ **Efficiency** of the pipe = 1 unit per hour.

⇒ Amount of water **emptied** in **5 hours** = Efficiency × Time = 1 × 5 = 5 units.

⇒ **Part** of the tank emptied = (Emptied units) ÷ (Total Capacity) = 5 ÷ 20 = 1/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a **pipe** can fill/empty a **tank** in x hours, then the part filled/emptied in **1 hour** is 1/x.

Combined Work Formula

If **Pipe A** fills in x hours and **Pipe B** empties in y hours, the net work in **1 hour** is (1/x − 1/y).

Work and Time Relationship

**Total Work** = Efficiency × Time. Efficiency is inversely proportional to the **time** taken to complete the work.

questions.question: P and Q together can complete a work in 12 days. R alone can complete the same work in 18 days. P, Q and R together can complete 1/3 part of the same work in how many days?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Let **Total Work** be LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 units. Efficiency of **(P+Q)** = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units/day. Efficiency of **R** = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units/day. Total Efficiency **(P+Q+R)** = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day. Work to be completed = 1/3 × 36 = 12 units. Time = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4 days. **∴ The correct answer is 2.4 days.**

questions.question: A car is moving at a speed of 90 km/hr. What will be the speed of the car in m/s?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To convert **speed** from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply the value by **5/18**.

Speed in m/s = 90 × (5/18)

⇒ 5 × 5 = 25 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 25 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the car = 90 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

1 **kilometer** (km) = 1000 **meters** (m)

1 **hour** (hr) = 3600 **seconds** (s)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/497f4af272b7f5d322d78cb9347cce4640431246cc747f214c6b3134f5dd4a11.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed = 90 × (1000 m / 3600 s)

⇒ Speed = 90 × (10 / 36) m/s

⇒ Speed = 90 × (5 / 18) m/s

⇒ Speed = 5 × 5 m/s

⇒ Speed = 25 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 25 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

m/s to km/hr Conversion

To convert speed from **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply the value by **18/5**.

Average Speed

Average Speed = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**. For two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x+y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (u − v). In **opposite directions**, it is the **sum** (u + v).

questions.question: G travels from P to Q. H travels from Q to P. They start travelling at the same time. Distance between P and Q is 390 km. They meet at point S after 3 hours. Speed of G is 80 km/hr. What is the speed (in km/hr) of H?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Relative Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Meeting Time **Relative Speed** = 390 ÷ 3 = 130 km/hr Since they move in **opposite directions**, **Relative Speed** = Speed of G + Speed of H 130 = 80 + Speed of H Speed of H = 130 − 80 = 50 km/hr **∴ The correct answer is 50 km/hr.**
